Subject: Compact network narrative & evidence (SOC 2 / SIG)

Hi Alice / GreenBank security team,

Following up on our onboarding checklist for the SIG and SOC 2 review: attached is a compact set of artifacts we can provide that map our network isolation model for Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments into the SIG/CAT control structure. The goal here is to give reviewers three concise artifacts they can use without wading through the full architecture binder.

Requested deliverables (we will supply):
- A 1-page diagram (control plane / data path / management plane) with annotated isolation boundaries and egress routes (attachment: network-compact-diagram.pdf).
- An index CSV mapping each diagram element to SIG questions and SOC 2 criteria (attachment: evidence-index.csv).
- A short control plane matrix describing routing, RBAC, and KMS boundaries (attachment: controlplane-matrix.md).

Clarifying notes we will include on the diagram:
- Dedicated pools are in tenant-isolated VPCs with strict egress proxies and zero shared storage across tenants.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) has a customer-controlled control plane path; we annotate optional airgap/edge-proxy options.
- Management plane is logically separated; access is via bastion + MFA + ephemeral certs and logged to our audit pipeline.

Could you confirm if this compact set will satisfy the initial SIG submission for GreenBank (HubSpot GB-188)? If you need any additional callouts (e.g., specific CIDR ranges, FIPS-validated KMS references, or hardware HSM statements), let us know and we will add them.

Can we target COB Thu 2027-10-07 for your initial review comments?

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Head of Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The compact pack looks like the right shape. A couple of clarifying asks from our side before we share with the audit team:

1) Can you explicitly call out where customer data traverses public networks for Private deployments (VPN vs direct connect) and how we can demonstrate encryption-in-flight controls?
2) For Dedicated pools, can you add a short note on how KV cache persistence is handled (is any tenant data ever written to shared disks)?
3) Do you have a short statement that lists the KMS providers and whether HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise customers?

If you can answer inline and send a small updated PDF we can push this to our reviewers tomorrow morning.

Best,

Subject: Re: Compact network narrative & evidence (SOC 2 / SIG)

Alice — quick answers inline and attached a patched PDF and a short FAQ snippet (see controlplane-matrix.md).

1) Public network traversal (Private deployments):
- Private (VPC) supports both VPN (IPSec) and Direct Connect/ExpressRoute. In both modes we enforce TLS 1.3 on the application layer. For VPN we add an additional IPSec tunnel; for Direct Connect the link is within the cloud provider network — we document the handoff points in the diagram. The compact PDF marks the likely handoff (edge-proxy) and we include sample TLS cipher suites.

2) KV cache persistence for Dedicated:
- KV caches are in-memory by default and sharded per-tenant in the serving runtime. We do not persist KV cache shards to shared disks for Dedicated tenants. Checkpointing for long-running jobs (optional) is to tenant-scoped object stores; anything written is tagged with tenant ids and encrypted at rest. The diagram includes an annotation and the evidence-index references the config toggle that disables checkpointing.

3) KMS / HSM statement:
- We support cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) and offer HSM-backed keys via Cloud HSM/CloudKMS options for enterprise contracts. We have a short statement in controlplane-matrix.md and can generate an exportable record for audit if the reviewers require a vendor-signed attestation.

I've attached: network-compact-diagram_v2.pdf (updated handoff markers), controlplane-matrix.md (FAQ lines added), evidence-index.csv (added field mappings).

Will follow up on specific CIDR ranges in a separate secure channel if you want exact values.

—Rishi
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
